title: What Happened to the Smurl Family After Their Horrifying Paranormal Encounters?
excerpt: The Smurls lived a normal life in Pennsylvania — then they claimed a demon began terrorizing their home
content:
NEED TO KNOW

  • The Smurl family consisted of patriarch Jack, matriarch Janet and their four daughters: Heather, Dawn, Shannon and Carin

  • Between the 1970s and 1980s, the Smurls began reporting paranormal activity in their Pennsylvania home and sought help from the Catholic Church and Ed and Lorraine Warren

  • The 2025 film The Conjuring: Last Rites was inspired by the Smurl family’s experiences

The Conjuring: Last Rites was inspired by the Smurls.

Before what they claim was a haunting, the family led a quiet, normal life just outside of Wilkes-Barre, Pa. In fact, they lived in their West Pittston duplex for years before the strange occurrences started, and those instances led them to call paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren for help.

The Conjuring franchise’s 2025 release follows Ed (Patrick Wilson) and Lorraine (Vera Farmiga) as they take on a demon that terrorizes patriarch Jack Smurl (Elliot Cowan) and his wife Janet Smurl (Rebecca Calder), while also targeting their four daughters: Heather (Kila Lord Cassidy), Dawn (Beau Gadsdon), Shannon (Molly Cartwright) and Carin (Tilly Walker).

The case marked the last the Warrens took on together, and Last Rites seems to be the final film for Wilson and Farmiga in the Conjuring universe.

So what happened to the family who inspired The Conjuring: Last Rites? Here’s everything to know about the Smurls’ experiences and where they are today, decades after their lives changed forever.

What is the story of Jack and Janet Smurl?

Jack and Janet moved into their house in West Pittston, Pa., in October 1973. During an interview with Lorraine, the couple shared they began experiencing paranormal activity in the home in 1985.

Janet told Lorraine the first occurrence was the night of their daughter Heather’s confirmation on April 9, 1985.

Janet, Shannon and Heather were in the kitchen, and Janet was pinning the collar onto Heather’s confirmation robe when a ceiling light, affixed with two chains and several eye hooks into a beam, crashed down onto the kitchen table without warning.

“It was very frightening because it was unexpected and it wasn’t like a light that had broken naturally,” Janet recalled. “It didn’t tip, it didn’t sway — it just came crashing down. It gouged Shannon in the forehead and left a mark on the refrigerator.”

Subsequently, Janet claimed the family heard and witnessed other unexplained activity, including doors opening, closing and unlocking by themselves and lights turning on and off. In particular, the accordion-style closet door in Jack and Janet’s bedroom opened and shut rapidly on its own. They also heard loud banging and pounding in threes, and items went missing.

According to the 2020 documentary Devil’s Road: The True Story of Ed and Lorraine Warren, Jack and Janet claimed their bed shook, and they saw a black shadow lurking in their bedroom. In another instance, Janet was reportedly yanked out of bed. On a different night, the couple levitated “as high as the ceiling,” Ed recalled.

The Wilkes-Barre Times Leader reported that the family also experienced foul odors and heard pig grunts in the home. The occurrences grew more aggressive over time, with the Smurls’ 75-lb. German shepherd getting slammed into a wall and Jack getting attacked while praying.

Jack also claimed to have been sexually assaulted by the spirit, which Ed later deemed a succubus, on several occasions.

How did Ed and Lorraine Warren get involved in the Smurl haunting?

Jack and Janet initially sought help from their local Catholic Church.

“We went to our local priest and said, ‘Father, there’s something very strange going on here,’ ” Janet recalled on Larry King Live. “So he came over, he blessed the home and said, ‘There’s no one here who can help you.’ ”

They then reached out to the Warrens by phone for assistance. Ed and Lorraine attempted to vanquish the succubus with prayer, crosses and holy water, and they had a police officer with them for protection.

Ed claimed the demon attacked him and “threw [him] back 10 feet” and declared it too strong for them to defeat on their own. They approached the Catholic Church again for help, but were denied once more. Ed took to the media to appeal to the church and asked for “two or three priests” to exorcise the demon.

“You can not even imagine what has gone on in this home,” Lorraine said in a press conference.

Lorraine determined there were four spirits haunting the Smurl house: three human entities and one demon.

Public pressure aided the Smurls and Warrens — Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger, who would later become Pope Benedict XVI in 2005, assigned an exorcist to the case. According to Ed, the exorcist went to the Smurls’ home and performed an exorcism on the property, and the home has been “clear” ever since.

What happened to the Smurl family’s house?

The Smurl family’s house is still standing in West Pittston, per Realtor.com.

According to The Citizens’ Voice, the Smurls moved to Jack’s nearby hometown of Wilkes-Barre, Pa., in 1988.

Richard Bridle purchased the property as a rental unit, but he initially had difficulty finding tenants due to the home’s notoriety.

“It’s hurting me as far as renting the property. There is a stigma attached to the house,” Bridle told UPI, adding that he thought the haunting claims were “ridiculous.”

Debra Owens, who moved into the Chase St. house in 1988, told the Wilkes-Barre Times Leader she never experienced anything unusual in the house, and a man who lived on the other side of the duplex home also said he saw no strange occurrences while residing there.

Where is the Smurl family now?

The patriarch of the family, Jack, led a quiet life after becoming a reluctant media sensation from the hauntings. He worked for the Topps Chewing Gum company in Duryea, Pa., for over 30 years and remained active in his local church.

Jack died from diabetes complications on June 22, 2017, according to an obituary. He was 75.

His daughter Carin told The Citizens’ Voice at the time, “It was so quick. We didn’t expect it because he had been doing so well. He told my mom ... one of his biggest regrets was that he wasn’t going to make it to their 50th anniversary.”

After Jack’s death, Janet married Charles Albert Dilworth in April 2021. They were together until she died at home on Jan. 10, 2026, at the age of 78, per an obituary.

As for the couple’s daughters, the older two live private lives. Heather is a mom to two adult children and is a teacher in Wilkes-Barre. Dawn also raised her son Mark Glowinski II in Wilkes-Barre, and he has gone on to play as a guard in the NFL for the Seattle Seahawks, New York Giants and Indianapolis Colts, WVIA News reported.

As for the twins, Shannon has also lived outside of the public eye and works in healthcare, per her LinkedIn, though she revealed on X (formerly Twitter) in December 2020 that she’s still interested in the paranormal and ghost hunting.

Carin is a social work professional. She has maintained that the family did not fabricate the hauntings.

“That we did it for fame or money is the most ridiculous statement ever. We were a normal family with normal lives that went through a tragedy and prevailed by staying strong and faithful,” she told The Citizens’ Voice in August 2016. “It’s everyone else that blew it up into a nightmare. We battled the demons inside and the public outside. They made it worse.”

She added, “We never made money from the book or movie. Who would want to go through all that media and public bashing?”

Carin is also a part-time paranormal investigator, an endeavor she pursued because of what she endured as a child.

“The reason I have been involved in paranormal investigating is so no one has to go through what we did,” she said. “In me, they get judge-free, discreet, legitimate, honest, professional help and counseling. No one going through tragedy should be treated like we were.”

More recently, she watched The Conjuring: Last Rites and had some thoughts on the 2025 film at the time of its release.

“They wrapped [the franchise] up well as a fan, but as a family I don’t know why they wasted our time even talking to us and stressing that they wanted to tell our story accurately and compassionately,” she wrote on Facebook, per The Citizens’ Voice.
